messages.subject: Preliminary Baseline Polling Memorandum
messages.body:
McGee,

Please find attached a copy of the questionnaire with comments from some of our colleagues.

We should consider the following issues in the questionnaire:
1. Drug and alcohol abuse. National survey of drug users completed recently indicates there are 7500 active drug users, only 174 persons can be treated at any given time in the current facilities.
2. Infrastructure: sewerage systems, safe water and harbors. Currently roughly one fifth of government budget on these projects. Everywhere we go that seems to be the demand along with good quality education and health care.
3. Population concentration. Majority of islands with populations under 1000. 64 out of 196 inhabited islands with less than 100 residents in total. Per capita cost of providing services to these small islands is prohibitive compared to their relocation to bigger islands. Issue is sensitive because people don't like moving to other islands unless there is an incentive package including new homes and financial compensation.
These issues also need to be reflected in the questions.

For next Friday meeting, Shafeeu will be in Sri Lanka, but we will try to bring him

and Jeff Waheed into the discussion.
Best regards
Waheed

Tunisia: Tunisia's transition suffered a terrible blow on February 6th when leftist opposition alliance founder and head of the Democratic Patriots party Chokri Belaid was shot dead outside his home in Tunis. The event drew thousands of protesters to the streets, claiming against the leaning Islamist Ennahda party. The events heighten the Islamist-secular divide that has featured heavily in Tunisian politics since the fall of the Ben Ali regime in 2011. The Islamist-led government described the event as the “assassination of the Tunisian revolution” and promised to dissolve the Islamist-led government and form a technocrat government aimed at promoting national unity at this divisive time.

Egypt: The second anniversary of the Egyptian revolution on January 25th was marked less by celebration than it was by violence, culminating in a week of unrest that took the lives of more than 50 people. The week was also marked by the imposition of a curfew, state of emergency, and large military deployment in the cities of Suez, Ismailia, and Port Said. The events reflect the disillusionment of Egyptians, given the lack of progress on both political and economic fronts, and the inability of the government to provide security. The violence has also highlighted the role that the army—the country’s most powerful institution—warned of the “collapse of the state” is a telling and serious message, conveying the institution’s growing frustration with the political impasse.

The recent violence has also generated serious economic losses and fuel shortages, and caused yet another delay with the much-needed IMF loan. It will be interesting to see how the recent violence—as well as the general malaise caused by economic woes—affects the Muslim Brotherhood’s performance in the upcoming parliamentary election (which is yet to be scheduled). A recent report issued by the Brotherhood’s political bureau hinted that the party’s popularity has been in decline.

Against this backdrop of political and economic turmoil, the 12th summit of the Organization of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) convened in Cairo on February 5th with a number of key players in the region in attendance—among them President Gul of Turkey, Emir Hamad al-Thani of Qatar, and Saudi Crown Prince Salman. The summit aimed to discuss Syria, Mali, and the Palestinian issue. The spotlight, however, was on Mahmoud Ahmadinejad: the first Iranian president to visit Egypt since the 1979 Islamic revolution.

Libya: On January 31st, European Union foreign policy chief Catherine Ashton announced the launch of a two-year civil mission to help secure Libya’s 4,000-kilometer border. The announcement was complemented by a surprise visit to Tripoli by David Cameron, who also announced his government’s commitment to helping the Libyan military and police with training and support. Furthermore, a meeting in Paris the week of February 11th will bring together a number of countries to discuss security cooperation and the future of the Libyan legal system. These initiatives are a telling manifestation of the urgent need to address security in Libya—especially border security—given the Mali crisis, the recent terrorist incident in Algeria, and concerns about security and stability across North Africa.

Jordan: The results of the Jordanian parliamentary election came as no surprise: pro-government candidates strengthened their hold, though state television reported that the majority of the 150 seats had been won by independents (an indicator that tribal allegiance is becoming a more important factor than party politics). According to official figures, 56 percent of the country’s 2.3 million registered voters turned out for the ballot, with the most obvious being that of the Muslim Brotherhood, which protested what it considered to be a biased ballot. It remains unclear who will succeed Prime Minister Abdallah Ensour (who submitted his resignation to King Abdullah on January 29th); although analysts and commentators consider it likely that a number of unexpected appointments will be made in an effort to address the growing malaise. Media reports indicate that there are also plans to set up an official channel for communication with the Muslim Brotherhood, perhaps in an effort to address the group’s concerns and bring it back into the political fold. In the meantime, the King made visits to Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, and Kuwait from January 29th to February 4th.

Syria: Israeli warplanes are generally believed to have struck a convoy en route to Lebanon on January 30th, although this has not been confirmed by the government of Israel. The convoy was reported to have been carrying sophisticated antiaircraft weaponry to Hezbollah. The attack—carried out on the outskirts of Damascus—was met by a sharp threat of retaliation from both the Syrian and Iranian governments; a significant indicator of the regional reverberations of the Syrian civil war and the general volatility permeating the region.

Despite the lack of progress of an international peace initiative spearheaded by Special Envoy Lakhdar Brahimi, a new plan by Syrian opposition leader Moaz al-Khatib—comprising a dialogue with President al-Assad on the principle of the regime’s departure—offers a glimmer of hope. Upon meeting with al-Khatib on February 3rd, the ministers of Iran and Russia (the closest allies of the al-Assad regime) seem to have agreed to help facilitate this process—an interesting turn of events. The new plan comes as the humanitarian situation continues to deteriorate, although some help is foreseen from the $1.5 billion in pledges made at a donors’ conference on January 30th in Kuwait.

messages.body:
B did 4 hours of work with Bill yesterday morning. He rested the afternoon but then insisted on going out for dinner (!!) and then got a migraine and left within a few minutes.

I just don't think it is wise for him to be up and pushing it so hard. It makes no sense to me why he goes full court press on diagnosis and treatment but will have suboptimal results due to compliance. It's not like this is just a finger. It's his vision. Geez.

Anyway, Sam continues to be whiny and emotional and I think driving Boris to get up and out more.

Docs have told him to not look up or put his head in certain positions but when you are out about you can't control these things because of the reflexes connected to your neck muscles. Your eyes move reflexively, like when you look down to walk down stairs your eyes are actually looking up. You get it...voluntary control of eye movements is "easier" when you aren't moving around so much. He thinks I am nagging at him.

He showed me the retinal and vascular imaging which I only have a rudimentary understanding - just the vascular side. I don't look at a lot of retinal images. Anyway, his macula is pretty much gone on the R. Maybe that is why he's kind of given up (or feels that way to me) since peripheral vision returning is just so so, and also not even guaranteed. Contribution to binocular vision with just periphery is pretty minimal. And virtually no contribution to depth since it screws with accommodation reflex to not see centrally.

Sam will be going to NYC next weekend.

Mette is coming in about 2.5 weeks.

That's the report for the past 24 hours from the Land of Boris.

messages.subject: Happy Birthday
messages.body:
Hi Jeff

Happy Birthday. Also thanks for the coffee (Jennifer is a superb brewer). In looking back at my class notes, you may be interested in Nabokov s first-day of instructions to the students in Lit 311 on Monday, September 14, 1953, the first day of his day of teaching at Cornell. It was also my first lecture course. After telling us to take (and stay in) assigned seats in the lecture hall (which had about 300 seats), and introducing <REDACTED> who sat on a chair on stage facing him, as the course assistant, he said what we, readers, needed to read novels was 1) a good memory 2) artistic feelings, and 3) a good dictionary. He then said it was a fatal mistake, though a current trend in academia, to search for historical or social meaning because a great novel is a pure invention by the author, and like nature, a deception. He also warned against identifying with any of the characters/ Instead, he said we should be looking for a tingling in the spine. The author were enchanters, and created their effects by orchestrating details that evoked pictures in our head.

I don't think I ever got through The Gift, though, fdollowing his instructions, I bathed myself in the details

Best regards

Ed Epstein

messages.body:
Speed by which is spreading is amazing. It is now coming it WSJ and few others.

And it was not even coordinated - it was actually worked to stop it.

Bill Gates Invests In Cancer DNA Sequencing Firm
Matthew Herper - Forbes

"Advances in understanding the human genome are having a dramatic impact on almost every area of medicine. Foundation Medicine's approach in harnessing the power of genomic data to improve care for cancer patients could represent an extremely important step forward in improving routine cancer care. I'm happy to be supporting this quite promising approach."

With those words in a press release this morning, Bill Gates, the world's second-richest man, announced that he was investing in Foundation Medicine, a Cambridge, Mass.-based company that sells a $5,800 diagnostic test that uses DNA sequencing to help doctors guess which cancer drugs would be helpful in fighting a particular patient's tumor.

Foundation, which previously listed Kleiner Perkins Caulfield & Byers and Google Ventures, raised $13.5 million in the series B round in which Gates participated, bringing its total take to $56 million. The other investors were Facebook billionaire Yuri Milner, who also recently invested in the personal genomics company 23andMe, and Russian investment firm Rusnano, which acquired DiGene, which was sold to Qiagen for $1.6 billion in 2007. Jones will also join Foundation's board.

Founded in April 2010 by Third Rock Ventures, Foundation is one of the first companies to aim to take advantage of the explosion in DNA sequencing technology, which has been cheaper and more powerful at a rate that exceeds the famous Moore's Law that drives the constant increases in microchips and computers. The company has raised $1,000 to get a fairly accurate readout of the 6 billion letters of DNA code for any single person.

In cancer, the approach right now is usually not to sequence all a patient's DNA or that of his tumor, but instead to focus on particular genetic mutations in the tumor that might provide clues as to what medicines to try. Major cancer centers are using this approach with patients for whom it's not obvious which medicine represents the best bet. Foundation's approach has been to kind of testing to a larger audience. To do so, it uses the DNA sequencing machines made by Illumina and other companies.

"What we want to do is take this testing to the community practices to treat patients where they live," Michael Pellini, Foundation's chief executive, told me in 2011.

There is some evidence backing that up. In a study conducted with the Dana-Farber Cancer Institute and published in Nature Medicine, found that more than half of patients with lung and colon cancer might benefit from the test.

It is difficult to analyze DNA data. Foundation's test is anything but a full genome, as it quoted previously, it's a $6,000-02% of the genome, showing how much of the problem of using genetic information will need to coming from solving computational and analytical problems — exactly the kind of thing that Bill Gates has always been interested in both at Microsoft and in his work getting lifesaving vaccines to children all around the world.

Gates has a longstanding interest in biotechnology. In 2001, BusinessWeek called Gates' 'other passion,' noting his large stake and board seat in ICOS, since sold to Eli Lilly, and his investment in a Seattle cancer drug company called Corixa. But lately Gates' interest has seemed more focused on the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, and when he mentioned in drug industry circles it is usually genomics for his work in global health. Could this be a change? It's a small investment, especially for Gates; we'll just have to wait and see.

messages.subject: My new blog " Inspiring Sweetness "
messages.body: Inspiring Sweetness. What inspires your life? January My Dear Friend, I am writing to you from Paris on my birthday week, having brought myself here to quite honestly, spoil myself a little, to fill my cup with all the sweetness and beauty of this special place that never fails to inspire me. We're constantly in a process of reinvention, especially as women, if we are determined to live an awakened life in conscious pursuit of what we love, each day gives us the opportunity to achieve greatness. This week in particular I find myself in the thralls of that process, saying goodbye to the old and welcoming in the new. Spirituality for me means nothing more than setting aside a little quiet time to connect with my inner self, honoring the reflective aspect we each have inside, that which listens to what makes us tick and pays attention to it. It's purely undemoninational, has zero do to with religion and all to do with being grateful. I'm reminded of a quote a friend recently posted on Facebook which I love: "The smile on my face doesn't mean my life is perfect, it's because I'm grateful for what I have, and for what God has blessed me with." This perfectly sums up how I feel in this moment. Does it resonate with you as well? If we shy away from the word spiritual, we might instead use the word, "resonance." Resonance for example is the reason I'm writing to you in this format right now. For the longest time, I have shied away from posting my inner most thoughts on the chalkboard of life. It felt

vain, presumptive, like ' who am I ' to spurt out what I think about things and assume someone gives a 's', but I realize now that it's part of being in the big conversation of it all.
THE SAUCE with our company postings about books, events and spirituality for kids will still continue, and now, for six months I'll add something more uniquely personal. It's an experiment like all of life, so if you like my musings, please post a comment and I'll continue to write. It's good to know that someone's reading!! Many of you out there who will have glanced this over I know are full of insight, so please share your wisdom and inspiration and let this become an extended forum for how we can support each other in consciously creating the lives that we love.
I'll be sharing with you under my pseudonym (a.k.a) Chocolate Sauce not because it is playful and quirchy, which I am , but because I wholeheartedly believe in the power of surrendering the ego-fueled self and reconnecting to our inner source ' sauce ' of love, light and wisdom.
Soon I'll be heading back to my tiny Swan Cave in New York City, back to groceries and laundry and the humdrum of how to get ahead and stay gentle and kind in a city that doesn't honor the sensitive and the subtle.
Beauty and the spirit are closely linked, and whether or not the dream is fully realized, there are many beautiful elements in my life that, if I live with present awareness, will reveal themselves to me.
One in particular I'm experiencing in this moment is the fabulously, fun, loving and supportive nature of my girlfriends. I'm filled with such gratitude every morning to have such amazing women in my life.
There is beauty in the big and small things that we take for granted and taking time to savor our own inner being will help us live with an increased appreciation for the richness and joy that exists in our every day.
The surest way to get what we want is to be grateful for what we have.
Wishing you all the positive energy, inspiration and intuition that you need to manifest whatever it is you want to create with your life in 2013!!
And kickstart your life in the direction of your Dreams...

messages.body: yes, you are safe. w

I have been crying all night. It's amazing that I went to the Museum of the Moving Image benefit honoring Hugh Jackman, and worked my magic in half an hour with Universal's CEO Ron Meyer, 'Les Mis' creator Cameron Macintosh, Hugh Jackman and Anne Hathaway...getting the entire cast to perform at Friday's LA premiere after party. What took me 30 minutes table hopping would have taken the Universal corporate snails a month of emails...if they could think of it. I convinced all the studio executives that the only way they can touch the heart and minds of the academy to vote for 'Les Mis' for Best Picture is to have the cast sing live to them after the screenings. Those glorious voices resonate in the soul of the voter live. I have been working on this 24/7 for a month and seem to be the only creative astute thinker in the bunch. Having explained the intricacies of what I actually do...I now tell you I came home and cried all night because of Philip Michaels. Against your advice, I did speak to him at 6:30pm and practically begged him to have some empathy for me and just address my case and be done with me. I actually apologized for not having enough money to attract his interest. I said I accepted the case and to please help me...saying this is all the money I have in the world. He said he spent 15 minutes on the phone with you and there is nothing to be done. This guy has to be the most self serving lawyer in existence...or is that redundant for a lawyer. I can't thank you enough for all your kindness. I can't imagine what I would have done with out you. I am still in shock that Gary had my mother change the will for another $250,000 on her death bed on Dec. 10th. before her Feb. passing. Every time I went to see her lying in the hospital she knew she was handing Gary money until she drew her last breath. She was completely dishonest with me my whole life. This is such devastating information. The sick joke is that she really would have loved seeing my four pages on Dec. Harper's Bazaar...and that would have justified her support of the weaker son. It is also devastating that a woman who made her way in life resting on her beauty and feeling entitled to her husband's money would not have any empathy for another woman, her own daughter who worked since 16. Can we really get the money that is my birthright? This is the most sickening thing I ever went thru. xoxo Peg

messages.subject: How to Live: Autumn Talks on Breathing, Remembering, Dreaming, Sleeping, Speaking in Public, Eating Healthily, Mastering Busyness and Being Mindful.
messages.body:
This is an unmissable opportunity to hear the world famous philosopher Michael Sandel address the outstanding question of our age: how do we want to live together?

He has been called the most effective communicator of ideas in English, our most relevant living philosopher, a genius, a humanitarian, who can has taken philosophy into the global public domain and empowered audiences worldwide to participate in the highest quality of debate. His Harvard Justice course has become legendary. In Britain, BBC R4 audiences will know him as the Public Philosopher.

Evening Event, 6:30pm-7:45pm
how to: Thrive in a World of Too Much: Mastering Busyness
with Tony Crabbe

It is difficult to ask anyone 'How are you doing?'

without hearing the word 'busy' at some point in the answer... We feel overwhelmed by busyness because of the demands on our time; but busyness isn't just a fact of modern life, it's also a brand. Busyness isn't essential. Yes, there is a lot to do, but believing you are busy is both false and unhelpful. The answer to do is to thrive we have to respond differently to our world of too much, which starts with stopping managing our time and becoming less productive, deliberately.

Evening Event, 6:30pm-8:30pm
how to: Know what we should Eat (and ensure we lose Weight too)
with Vicki Edgson

The question on everyone's lips is: Just exactly WHAT should I be eating that's a) safe, b) nutritious, and c) will ensure I lose weight?

Whether its the 5:2, the 16:8, the South Beach, or the Paleo, at least 60% of adults in Britain will have been on a diet at some point, and over half of those are on continuous diets. Scary figures, which would be fine if they were achieving their goals BUT, it's estimated that 95% of people who lose weight on a diet is quite sure of WHAT they should be eating WHEN and WHY!

Evening Event, 6:30pm-8:30pm
how to: Remember
with Ed Cooke

An introduction to the imaginative techniques and stories behind the ancient arts of memory. Ed will lead an interactive, practical tour through the world of memory techniques, with numerous examples of how to boost your memory, how to forget and how to make sense of memory in the modern world.

LOS ANGELES (CN) - An investment fund claims it was swindled by a self-described "master illusionist" who persuaded it to invest in rare books and art - including a portrait of Sir Isaac Newton - and then absconded with more than $543,000 and a bunch of the loot.

Ensign Consulting Ltd. of the Virgin Islands, claims lead defendant Adam Seckel spent years crafting a persona with the assurance of responsibility before he approached one of its consultants about an investment in rare antique globes.

Four months later, Seckel claimed to have sold the globes for a 20 percent profit, splitting the proceeds 50-50 with Ensign, according to the complaint.

"Seckel then informed Ensign that he was also selling a consultant (nonparty) Adam Gold that he was 'at a chateau, whose believe it or not, the owner has an enormous collection of antiquarian science books inherited from her dad,' according to the Superior Court complaint.

"It is a stunning collection. I am trying to negotiate it out now, but will only do so at a price that makes a lot of sense," the complaint states, citing Seckel.

"Seckel then tried to persuade Ensign to invest in the books. Ensign agreed, and Seckel claimed to have bought the books for $68,000, according to the complaint.

Ensign says Seckel claimed he already had a buyer for the painting: Nathan Myhrvold, the former chief technology officer for Microsoft (Myhrvold is not a party to the complaint.)

Ensign says it gave Seckel $168,000 to buy the Newton portrait, and Seckel otherwise had no ownership interest in the Newton portrait, according to the complaint.

But that sale never happened, Ensign says.

Ensign says Seckel offered the Newton portrait to another defendant, Michael Sharpe Rare & Antiquarian Books, as collateral for a debt that Seckel Sharp for a 16th century manuscript.

"Since Ensign paid for and owned the Newton portrait and Seckel otherwise had no ownership interest in the Newton portrait, Seckel had no right to pledge the Newton portrait as collateral for his personal debt owed to Michael Sharpe," the complaint states.

Sharpe foreclosed upon the security interest in the Newton portrait, and with the court enforcing the judgment, promptly sold it to a third party, defendant Lou Weinstein, according to the complaint.

Ensign claims that everyone involved knew that it owned the portrait, and conspired to hide that fact from Ensign.

Sharpe made more than $284,000 on the transaction, and Seckel netted more than $15,000, the complaint states.

Meanwhile, Ensign claims, Seckel induced it to invest in eight sets of rare books that he described as either 'pre-sold,' or as good as 'pre-sold.'

But once again, Ensign says, the sales never took place.

Ensign says it entered into a contract with Seckel that required him to repay the price of the investments should any 'material adverse change' occur.

Ensign claims Seckel's double-dealing, Ensign says.

With weeks, Seckel said that three of the books, worth more than $100,000, had been stolen by a bookseller, though actually he had sold the books, using the bogus theft as a way to cover up his fraud, according to the complaint.

Finally, after Seckel defaulted, Ensign says it tried to take possession of the books and portrait, and hired an auction company to handle the sale.

At first Seckel failed to cooperate, then 'he finally admitted that he had pawned some of the books, presumably almost a year after having done so,' Ensign says.

Ensign says that in an email, Seckel said that he had pawned the books to comply with Ensign's demands for repayment.

Other defendants are Al Seckel, Isobel Maxwell, Illusionism LLC, Lou Weinstein, Heritage Book Shop, S. Krown & Sellman Booksellers, Michael Sharpe Rare & Antiquarian Books, W.P. Watson Antiquarian Books, and 19th Century Rare Book and Photograph Shop.

Ensign demands $543,259, and punitive damages for breach of contract, fraud, conversion, tortious interference with a contract, fraudulent transfer, negligent misrepresentation, and fraudulent accounting.

It is represented by Olivier Taillieu with Zuber & Taillieu.

messages.subject: ZDC - James
messages.body:
Hi Brice,

Thanks for the explanation. Upgrading to the AirPort Extreme 802.11ac base stations "could" help — they have a much stronger broadcast signal & range — but I have my doubts whether it will resolve the buffering issues while streaming.

Buffering issues are likely to come down to either bandwidth constraints or rebuffer issues (rebuffering is when you're streaming audio via Pandora or Spotify, etc. requires 5 Mbps bandwidth for each instance, video requires between 2 - 5 Mbps (depending on video quality), so if the boss and the girls are trying to Spotify at the same time, that's going to explain the full use of the T1 line (1.5 Mbps), and most likely the buffering / dropouts.

Upgrading the base stations won't anything. It's a tedious process of plugging one in and running ethernet from the base station to the router. If the base station is set up manually, it's a matter of an issue, the other 10% the base station has to be set up manually to the configuration of the device being replaced. It takes 10-15 minutes each for the tool, most of that is finding the existing base and an extra power outlet for the replacement.

Wireless relay is a way of bouncing network signals off existing base stations to other base stations that aren't close enough to a network port to hardware. Scott used this method a lot, and I've seen it work well in the past. The only caveat is that it requires a survey of the physical area around the base station's location — can't be done remotely.

messages.body:
What happens when your negotiation skills are really put to the test? You might negotiate on a daily basis, but can you deal with tough customers, and keep up with others who are looking to outmanoeuvre you? Are you certain that your solutions are the best they can be, or are there more creative win/win situations still to be unlocked?

How to: Advanced Negotiation is a direct and no-nonsense masterclass for those who want to negotiate smarter, harder and with greater dexterity. It assumes basic competence in the art of negotiation, and focuses on solving the tougher problems faced by negotiators using advanced techniques and exercises.

You'll learn how to deal with difficult negotiators and the classic negotiation gambits. You'll also develop a greater understanding of the psychological games that all humans play and how to use them to your advantage. Using case studies and practical role-play, you'll learn to handle toxic situations and sweep aside negotiation deadlock...

WORK - ADULTS

10.09.2014
Evening Event, 6.30pm-7.45pm
how to: Thrive in a World of Too Much: Mastering Busyness
with Tony Crabbe

It is difficult to ask anyone 'How are you doing?' without hearing the word 'busy' at some point in the answer. We feel overwhelmed by busyness and yet, paradoxically, we also crave it. Busyness is a fact of modern life, it's also a brand! Busyness isn't essential. Yes, there is a lot to do, but believing you're always busy because you have so much to do is both false and unhelpful. To thrive we have to escape the busyness trap. It starts with stopping managing our time and becoming less productive, deliberately.

Read more and book.

Anna Percy-Davis is on hand to help you work out what you want, and then put it into action. This morning workshop will be brimful of practical tips on networking, CV writing, interview techniques and getting the right work/life balance...

The testimony of victims is absolutely very sad. It's also inconsistent, and involves allegations that were brought to light under very dubious circumstances (previously estranged family members hiring civil lawyers for them, psychologists uncovering repressed memories, questionable investigative and interview techniques, etc).

No physical evidence. Mainly testimony by a handful of people who are now filing civil suits for millions, and a former football coach who has told numerous versions of his story (and is now filing a civil suit of his own). 2) BFP distributes cash pro rata to each owner of BFP LP
3) GRAT pays LDB annuity in cash and in-kind
4) New GRAT created every 3 months with aggregation of in-kind BFP LP interests paid to LDB (from earlier GRAT's).

messages.body: RJ, I.D., EA, AC, RD met with PW exchange attorneys and AH yesterday. We discussed the various options. Given that there may be more than one founder exchanging and given that each founder can choose different options to sell PTP interest, eg underwritten offering, secondary market, private sale and each founder can opt out at different times if price moves lower greater than 10% from Sept 4 closing price, there may be decisions one founder makes that has a effect on another founder. If there is an underwriting, and the underwriter prices with a significant discount, one founder can opt out (assume > 10% price decline) and wait for better price. Alternatively, the underwriter may decide to offer fewer shares in the offering and the scale back would be pro rata. However, if a founder opts out of underwriting then the other founder might not be scaled back despite the underwriter scale back. The underwritten offer has the greatest certainty of closing. We will be looking into the interaction of founders under the exchange agreement will the principals agree. If we detect that the exchange agreement does not cover a particular wrinkle or needs to clarify interplay of multiple founders exchanging concurrently, the agreement should be amended by Sept 4. Aug 29 is latest date to notify other founders of intention to exchange. Note that exchange agreement has been amended twice previously and that founders had noodeled (disclosed) with other founders far in advance of the deadline for notice.

messages.body: Also note that the mechanics of the exchange is that the underlying management company and carry GP entity vehicle interests are distributed up through AP Professionals to BRH Holdings to the member of BRH Holdings who then transfers these partnership interests to AP/A MH in exchange for PTP units. The exchange of property for PTP interest is taxable as a sale/exchange. The subsequent sale of PTP units gives rise to cash flow but not the large tax bite. So going into a 10b5-1 plan to sell has modest tax effect and does not serve to delay gain recognition. The APO Trading blackout recommences Dec 5 2014 but there is not blackout for 10b5-1 plan

messages.subject: only to you
messages.body:
Jeffrey,

I am very sorry about this. If I may explain what it is that I am doing, then hopefully we can fix this situation.

When I came to the island I saw one major problem. Landscaping was running from area to area and putting us fires, as directed by Ana. It was one problem area after the other.

So, I decided to split up the island so Ana took care of the homes, and I would get landscaping in shape. Irrigation is lacking, and as you can see when you look at the basket, and areas surrounding it. It looks much better now that irrigation is working.

I wanted to get all open projects done and get the crew into maintenance mode. As you can see, the engineering areas is no longer a junk yard, next week the tunnel will be organized with racks and all workshops clean and neat.

Infrastructure is paramount in my experience. When all is clean and neat, it is easier to maintain it that way.

I know this makes me a construction manager, but that is what I deemed the most important initial role in order to get 5 star service.

Regarding the tennis court, I was told that as long as it was ready by early September, it was all good. So, that is why you have not seen full action this past week up there. Other projects were demanding the full staff. I will get on the court next week and get it done.

The kite house. No excuse there. It's a mess, and Ana told me that we are waiting for windows and you knew about that.

Trampoline is filthy. Absolutely. Agree. I've asked Carlos to clean it 3 times and I will have to be more firm with him.

Let me get the things sorted out and then be more active in supervising Ana in her tasks as well. I must say that compared to other homes I've managed over the years, cleanliness is pretty good at LSJ. So, that's why I felt that I could concentrate on landscaping for a while.

It takes a little time to learn the ins and outs of a new place. What I'm learning here is that it's not enough to tell people what to do.

I will be done with landscaping next week and will at the same time get more involved with the remaining areas of LSJ

Sorry about the long email.

Happy 4th

John

messages.body:
Jeffrey,

Many thanks for your very encouraging words yesterday morning. This is already a super interesting experiment (even with 50 spots), since I am looking at a whole ecosystem of companies and unassigned patents, and trying to figure out what is missing and what is the best way to fill in the gaps. For example, investors starting Helicos took Eric's advice over mine (even though he had zero sequencing technology invention experience and I had 26 years) -- so rather than a large founder's share in a new company (Helicos), my technology dribbled into an established company (CGI) from 2006-2012. CGI was sold for $117M in 2012, while Helicos went bankrupt.

Below is a first pass list of potential investments for the $10M. This may be more information than you wanted at this point (especially given the trade-off between jargon and brevity), but I am having so much fun, I just wanted to also include a few extra thoughts, in case they provide 'teaching moment' or post-mortem at some point.

$20,000 Supercentenarianstudy.com
$1,500,000 eGenesisBio.com
$1,000,000 Sensor-Selectors
$1,000,000 Protein stability & virus resistance
$1,000,000 Biofuels
$800,000 Aging reversal
$1,550,000 Next generation pathology
$250,000 Space Genetics
$200,000 Cold-resistant elephants
$2,500,000 2nd tranche

Total

$10,000,000

1) Supercentenarianstudy.com Thirty genomes collected so far on a small budget by James Clement. $200K would get 8% ownership of the company and allow another 30 genomes to be collected, sequenced and therapies patented.
2) eGenesisBio.com: Using CRISPR to engineer animals for resistance to infectious diseases and to act as transplantation donors for major organs (initially kidneys) to humans. Co-founded with Prashant Mali and Luhan Yang. Already has a couple of contracts and a some rented lab space. Lead by Luhan Yang.
3) Sensor-selector technology for optimizing commercial production of (bio)chemicals. Lead by Vassan Raman.
4) New redox-insensitive protein cross linking based on radically recorded bacterial genomes and/or Multi-virus-resistant organisms. We just published papers and patents on this. Lead by Dan Mandell.
5) Eliminating ecosystem pests and invasive species. Lead by Kevin Esvelt. This will probably be in the news on July 17. Business model similar to the relationship between Amyris and the Gates Foundation for manufacturing anti-malarial drugs.
6) Making human genetic disease models in organisms and aging reversal using CRISPR and other epigenetic reprogramming factors. Lead by Bobby Dhadwar and Eswar Iyer. Possibly mergeable with Supercentenarianstudy.com.
7) A new sequencing method capable of displacing part of the medical pathology imaging market and filling in the large gap in most plant and animal genome sequences. Lead by Rich Terry.
8) Genome engineering of humans for space. Seed money for patent fees, some lab tests and education efforts via p2pL. Lead by Ting Wu.
9) Making cold-resistant elephants via CRISPR, focusing on blood, subcutaneous fat and/or hair/wool (based on what is known about cold-resistant animals, Mammoth DNA, and human mutations). Economies could be like those of the woolly mammoths by George Church and Hendrick Poinar. Possibly mergeable with eGenesisBio.
10) The rest would be set aside as a second tranche for whichever of the above efforts makes best progress first.

--George

messages.body: speak or skype today?

Jeffrey,

Many thanks for your very encouraging words yesterday morning. This is already a super interesting experiment (even with $10M spent), since I am looking at a whole ecosystem of companies and unassigned inventions totally differently. Eye-opening to see how accustomed one can become to the status quo. I have been thinking about your question about Helicos. Eric's advice over mine in 2003 (even though he had zero sequencing technology invention experience and I had 26 years) so rather than a large founder's share in a new company (Helicos), my technology dribbled into an established company (CGI) from 2006-2012. CGI was sold for $117M in 2012, while Helicos went bankrupt.

Below is a first pass list of potential investments for the $10M. This may be more information than you wanted at this point (specifically given the trade-off between jargon and brevity), but I have tried to include a few sentences about each. Please provide any new extra thoughts, in case they provide "teaching moment" or post-mortem at some point.

1) Supercentenarianstudies.com Thirty genomes collected so far on a small budget by James Clement. $200K would get 8% ownership of the company and allow another 30 genomes to be collected, sequenced and therapies patented.

2) eGenesisBio.com: Using CRISPR to engineer animals for resistance to infectious diseases and to act as transplantation donors for major organs (initially kidneys) in humans. Co-founded with Prashant Mali and Luhan Yang. Already has a couple of contracts and a some rented lab space.

3) Sensor-selector technology for optimizing commercial production of (biochemicals). Lead by Vasan Raman.

4) New redox-intensive protein cross linking based on radically recorded bacterial genomes and/or Multi-virus-resistant organisms. We just published papers and patents on this. Lead by Dan Mandell.

5) Eliminating ecosystem pests and invasive species. Lead by Kevin Esvelt. This will probably be in the news on July 17. Business model similar to the relationship between Amrys and the Gates Foundation for manufacturing anti-malarial drugs.

6) Making human genetic disease models in organoids and aging reversing using CRISPR and other epigenetic reprogramming factors. Lead by Bobby Dhawan and Eswar Iyer. Possibly mergeable with Supercentenarianstudies.com

7) A new sequencing method capable of displacing part of the medical pathology imaging market and filling in the large gaps in most plant and animal genome sequences. Lead by Rich Terry.

8) Genome engineering of humans for space. Seed money for patent fees, some lab tests and education efforts via pgd. Lead by Ting Wu.

9) Making cold-resistant elephants via CRISPR, focusing on blood, subcutaneous fat and wool/hair (based on what is know about cold-resistant animals, Mammoth DNA, and human mutations). Economics could be like the American Lean which recently grew from a handful to 500,000 as a source of low cholesterol meat. Lead by George Church and Justin Quinn. Possibly mergeable with eGenesisBio.

The rest would be set aside as a second tranche for whichever of the above efforts makes best progress first.

--George

messages.subject: only to you
messages.body:
I like working here and will make the changes.

Let's have a quick talk about how many emails you want to receive about smaller items. My typical role is to filter communication to the principals so they don't have to get involved in daily maintenance questions (i.e. new headlight for Bobcat, a few new plants for the entrance)

My understanding is that Rich keeps you updated on those purchases, so I have not done that in order to keep email volume down.

I would like to think that you are the manager of a great resort , and I am the most important guest it ever had , ana said ? , I told , I thought , they were doing something else . is not what you and I would expect : I understand one plate of glass as ordered weeks ago , however every door in the kite house is in need of repair or replacement . I like you and want you to succeed, I dont send emails that often regarding things that need to get done , but I think when I do , they should take priority . cement slab in planter, for example.

The trampoline is entirely my fault. Yes, I am ultimately responsible for every item on the island, so no excuse for that one...

Monday I will sit down with Carlos and ask him if he wants to be treated like a responsible employee or a dumb worker who needs to be led to each project I want done. I also have to learn who is capable of doing what they are told and who just ignores it because of their seniority and place on the pecking order.

Two things are working against me, but I can deal with that:

1. The staff hates that there is supervision. It was nicer for them with only Ana because they could just coast along.
2. I've heard more than once that " There has been so many in my role and they don't last, so don't be offended if we want and see"

Anyway. I will be more diligent about tasks being completed and that your living areas takes first priority at all times.

I want to make this work.

Thanks

John

ask what was ordered , when ? , did you check that the trampolin had been cleaned if you had already had to tell him twice . if I you were running a hotel would any of those answers mean anything to a guest.

Not held in BVI. Just asked Carlos where the boat papers are. Carlos is a drama queen.

I have been to the Kite house and complained about the sad state of it. Ana told me you were aware that we were waiting for new windows.

sorry , but this makes no sense to me , why should I care about the tunnel being clean or the trampoline . is dirty , why should I care about engineering , if the kite house is not livable , and the glass is broken , and there are no handles how is it possible as a hotel manager that you have never been in the kite house, I believe we can work it out, but this makes no sense at all to me . my guest has also commented how shitty things are kept now : this is possibly a sabotage move against you , I am aware, I have been told that the trampoline were done before my holiday weekend , and the landscale at the man compound and at my

Jeffrey,

I am very sorry about this. If I may explain what it is that I am doing, then hopefully we can fix this situation.

When I came to the island I saw one major problem. Landscaping was running from area to area and putting out fires, as directed by Ana. It was one problem area after the other.

So, I decided to split up the island so Ana took care of the homes, and I would get landscaping in shape. Irrigation is lacking, and as you can see when you look at the basket, and areas surrounding it... It looks much better now that irrigation is working.

I wanted to get all open projects done and get the crew into maintenance mode. As you can see, the engineering area is no longer a junk yard, next week the tunnel will be organized with racks and all workshops clean and neat.

Infrastructure is paramount in my experience. When all is clean and neat, it is easier to maintain it that way.

I know this makes me a construction manager, but that is what I deemed the most important initial role in order to get 5 star service.

Regarding the tennis court. I was told that as long as it was ready by early September, it was all good. So, that is why you have not seen full action this past week. Other projects were demanding the full staff. I will get on the court next week and get it done.

The kite house. No excuse there. It's a mess, and Ana had told me that we are waiting for windows and you knew about that.

Trampoline is filthy. Absolutely. I've asked Carlos to clean it 3 times and I will have to be more firm with him.

Let me get the things sorted out and then be more active in supervising Ana in her tasks as well. I must say that compared to other homes I've managed over the years, cleanliness is pretty good at LSJ. So, that's why I felt that I could concentrate on landscaping for a while.

It takes a little time to learn the ins and outs of a new place. What I'm learning here is that it's not enough to tell people what to do.

I will be done with landscaping next week and will at the same time get more involved with the remaining areas of LSJ

Sorry about the long email.

Happy 4th

John

messages.subject: Introducing Boomerang Premium & New Features
messages.body:
Hello!
We're writing to let you know about the biggest update to Boomerang yet!
Over the past couple of years, you've sent us many feature requests that we wanted to address, but that we couldn't build due to infrastructure costs or limited development and support resources. Today, we're releasing several of those features as part of a new Boomerang plan - Boomerang Premium. But first...
Keyboard Shortcuts
Before we introduce the new plan, we'd like to announce that your most requested feature is now available for users on all plans - Keyboard Shortcuts! To enable them, click the Boomerang menu in the top right corner of Gmail, choose Settings, and check the keyboard shortcuts box there.
After enabling keyboard shortcuts in Boomerang Settings, just press 'p' while viewing a message to open the Boomerang menu. While composing a message, press CTRL/CMD S to open the Send Later menu. For more info on how they work, click the question mark next to the keyboard shortcuts option in the Boomerang Settings. We hope this will make using Boomerang even faster for those of you who prefer a keyboard-only email experience!
Now, onto the Premium Plan!
Boomerang Premium adds a collection of advanced features to the Boomerang experience. Here's a whirlwind tour of everything that the new plan includes.
The Boomerang Toolbox
As an email productivity company, we hear dozens of ways our customers wish email could work better every month. The Boomerang Toolbox is a library of powerful, customizable scripts that let you do just that. We're releasing some of these great ideas in lightweight ways. Here are a few of the scripts that the Toolbox contains today:
* Find and label all of the messages you've sent that haven't gotten a response in the past week.
* Set up a label that, when applied to an email, will make that email get Archived or Deleted after a few days. Combine this label with filters to automatically purge promotional email
* Our Boomerang the Web script lets you easily schedule an email to remind you to come back to a webpage at a later date.
We'll be adding to the Toolbox on a regular basis, and Premium subscribers have a special page where they can suggest new ideas and help us prioritize.
Boomerang Everything You Send (By Default)
We sometimes find ourselves quietly cursing because we sent out a message without remembering to let Boomerang remind us about it later. As a Premium subscriber, you can now set up a default Boomerang configuration that will automatically apply to every message you send.
If you're sending out a bunch of emails, and you want all of them to come back to your inbox if nobody responds after a week, set your options and start sending email. All your messages will be tracked!
You can also read receipts in all your messages, and even set your messages to return if they go unread by default.
Premium Support
During business hours, premium support includes live chat with our friendly support staff. During non-business hours, or if you prefer email, Premium support requests will go through a separate channel so that we can respond as quickly as possible.
For existing users, you'll continue to receive the same quality of customer support, with every email receiving a response from one of our staff directly. Premium support is a way for us to make our customer support experience even better; standard support will remain awesome!
Boomerang Insights
Learn more about how you use email, how it compares to others, and how to get even more from non-inbox. Boomerang Insights provides data about how you use Boomerang, actionable benchmarks, data feeds, and more!

messages.body:
Hi <REDACTED>

Sorry for the delayed response. We just got word from the IRB and we're finally ready to push forward with the YPO study.

I wanted to discuss a couple things with Jeffrey by phone at his convenience including:

1. getting a whole genome through Illumina puts him a little bit outside of the workflow pipeline for the YPO project. Ie, those participants are paying $1000 each and will be getting their exomes sequenced through Ambry, a thumbnail drive of their compressed genomic data, and an annotated report of 56 ACMG gene hits. I think it's worth it for Jeffrey to be able to get the same pipeline as the YPO folks and others in our study. Last time I discussed with him he definitely wanted a whole genomes through Illumina for ~$11,000 (which is still fine) but would he be interested in also getting the $1000 exome also through the normal pipeline? Although the exome data should be redundant with the whole genome data, it think it's worth it for the thumbnail drive and the ACMG gene summary. We'll also be able to check for concordance between the 2 datasets.

2. Jeffrey has samples (including fibroblast cell culture from his skin biopsy) at HMS. Do I have his permission to request these samples from the PGP for inclusion in the YPO study? (The samples can be used for both studies if he wishes.) Our YPO study may need a self-collected saliva sample for which I can mail him a kit. So, I wanted to discuss these sample issues with him as well.

3. Lastly, we are actually still need some informatician and genetic counselor support for the YPO study - not just for his sample but all of our 80 plus study subjects (from the Austin chapter). As I mentioned, all 80+ have already paid $1000 each for the sequencing but we still need to cover bioinformatics and a part-time GC for all participants. In the past, months ago now to the IRB delay, Jeffrey was generous enough to offer to pay for sequencing of YPO members. Since that's already covered now, would he still be able to cover the bioinformatics and genetic counseling for this study?

I'm available to discuss later this evening. Tomorrow and this weekend are also relatively open for a brief call. My cell is 917-774-3346.

Thanks in advance for passing on this message. We're excited to finally be moving forward with our innovative study.

Best,
Joe

messages.body:
Jeffrey,

Here are some ideas for the Dining Room...forgive the quick presentation...this is just the start.

Walls in chinoiserie with intricate carved gilded trim...perhaps holding lit porcelain figures or Lalique birds (note sure how you feel about birds)...the motifs and coloring in the chinoiserie will need careful study, perhaps we are considering a tone on tone palette with gilded figures (similar to tech Peacock Room)...perhaps the ceiling is eglomise panels, back painted glass...a luminous ceiling with chinoiserie details or perhaps astrological signs...or other...maybe we change the floor to wood to a beautiful inlay pattern (no central medallion)...and create two groups of seating, one with comfortable sofas/chairs, another with a dining table for 4 or 6...I still think it might be nice to keep a fireplace but change the scale, change the feeling of it entirely...

Let me know your thoughts...

My best,
Amy

If you agree, I'd like to set up an Experiment Room in the house, so that all of the samples can live there and you can see full scale mock ups (fabrics, carpet, wall and floor finishes) in various types of light to evaluate and debate before we decide to execute...think about it...maybe there's a spot we could use?

Jeffrey,

Walls in chinoiserie with intricate carved gilded trim...perhaps holding lit porcelain figures or Lalique birds (not sure how you feel about birds)...the motifs and coloring in the chinoiserie will need careful study. Let me know your thoughts...

My best,
Amy

Good afternoon Jeffrey,

I met with the two representatives from the Department of Education re the STEM Fair that is to take place at UVI in two weeks time. We originally agree to send the winners of the Fair to the US Science Fair in DC and we allocated $10K of the $86K for this purpose. I think the winning students will get more out of a trip if they were to attend a two week-long summer program. The STEM Coordinator for DOE has identified some summer programs that focus on each of the four pillars of STEM. However, it will obviously cost more to send the three winning students to a summer program. Would you approve an additional $10K for this purpose to cover the cost of the camp and airfare for the three winning students?

With warm regards,
Cecile

messages.subject: Trust investments-Fiduciary Duty
messages.body:
Hi Brad and Jeffrey,

Barry just called me to discuss his fiduciary duty in connection with the OWL investment and all investments generally. In his understanding that Leon's intention, as grantee of the various trusts, is for trust assets to be used for the benefit of his children, which includes helping them learn about investing. In that regard, he can see some basis for the Trustees-investing in OWL, an investment that interests the three boys. However, he has mixed feelings about putting the trust funds in a venture capital investment because of the risk factor (un-understanding of course, that the investment could do very well).

The bottom line of Barry's call is that he would feel more comfortable as a Trustee making such investments if:
1. Leon provided the Trustees with a Memorandum of Intention reminding the Trustees of the reasons for which he created the trusts w and the purposes for which he would approve of trust assets being used; and
2. We prepared a Trustee resolution articulating the reasons why the Trustees decided to make the investment (reciting the grantee-E2's intention as expressed in the memorandum).

Barry would also feel more comfortable if the children had more current information about, and were somewhat involved in, trust-investment decisions. Along the lines of Jeffrey's earlier suggestion, Barry would like to see the children get regular trust statements (he would be fine with quarterly). We also discussed the possibility of periodic accountings (again, as Jeffrey suggested) and Barry would like to hear more about that.

Please let me know how you would like to proceed and to respond to Barry. If you agree, I can prepare a Memorandum of Intention for Leon to sign in connection with the APOI Agreement and the APO2 Declaration. This is a non-binding document that is designed to give Trustees comfort in exercising their fiduciary discretion. It does not, of course, guard against a challenge by a beneficiary. The periodic accountings and releases should do that (assuming proper disclosure).

Shall we put the idea of quarterly beneficiary state=ents and periodic accountings on the Agenda for the next Trustees meeting?

messages.subject: Jeffrey - 4 trades I like - Nav [C]
messages.body: Classification: Confidential

Hi Jeffrey,
There hasn't been much I've really liked recently.
Here are four trades - 3 I like right now and 1 for now or soon.

1) BUY 10y BTPS @ 3.16% - This is a 3-6mth 'buy the rumour sell the fact' tactical trade to position for ECB QE (now)
The ECB is preparing both itself and markets for QE - Its senior board members have stepped up public comments over the past 48hrs. This is the clearest sign so far QE could happen and why I am writing to you now.
Ideally ECB wants to buy ABS from small to medium sized European companies but the outstanding available is relatively small so it will likely buy Eurozone Government Bonds. The spread between Italian BTPS and German Bunds has tightened significantly past 18months but old metrics of value make no sense in Europe because they rely on history when there was no QE.
While It's hard to get excited about 10y BTPS yielding 3.16% (164bp over 10Y German Bunds) I'd still have 5-10mm 10y BTPS in my portfolio both for the duration and spread compression potential. I prefer 10y over 5y because the recent nearly parallel spread compression has left 5s10s steep relative to 0-5s.

3 reasons i like this trade:
i) macro investors view ECB QE as a second bite at the cherry. Everyone i talk to wants European risk assets having seen QE in the US.
ii) ECB QE is probably still 3-6mths away which will keep credit bid.
iii) Credit has been bulledproof during the recent risk selloff because ECB QE expectations, b) G3 rate hikes are being pushed into the future while cash has nowhere else to go. This price action is telling as and when equities recover i think credit continues to tighten

2) Tactically position for higher EURUSD - 2 week view (now)
BUY EUR50mm 2week expiry 1.40 strike European Style EURUSD Calls @ 6bp (EUR30,000)
This is a low cost contrarian short term tactical call. Most investors myself included are bullish USD in the medium term (see trade 3) but in the very short term I see EURUSD higher because:
i) Despite ECB preparing the markets for QE, the price action of EURUSD (broadly unchanged) has been quite bullish compared to what one would expect
ii) Speculators don't appear long EURUSD to us. Majority are short or flat.
iii) implied volatility is 5.25% (offer for 2week options) which is very very low historically. So this is a penny option, highly convex, pain trade bet against other speculators betting on QE
If my view is wrong 6bp is lost. If i'm right i'd plan to exit in a week making 4-6x

iii) The dollar hasn't appreciated yet because short rates in the US haven't risen meaningfully
iv) THE KEY POINT - FX volatility is very low in currency pairs like EURUSD where central bank policy on each side is increasingly diverging
v) Low vol makes this bet inexpensive to put on.

messages.subject: Carbon Fiber Violin
messages.body:
We do ship internationally and I have some violins here that would LOVE to go to you. We would pay the shipping to you, as you might have to pay import taxes (and if you didn't want to keep it, the shipping back). The shipping is very expensive so you shouldn't order an instrument impulsively. We ship via FedEx International Priority for the safety of the instruments and under the terms of returning it, it would have to be shipped back the same way.

I only ship internationally at the beginning of each week so that the instrument will get there without having to spend a weekend in a warehouse. If I ship on Monday or Tuesday you would have it by the end of the week. Occasionally clearing customs takes longer than this, but usually not.

You can pay by check with a bank check in U.S. Dollars, or you can use VISA, MasterCard or American Express. You can just go on our website and charge the cello. If the charge doesn't go through, call the issuer bank of the credit card. As it is such a large amount of money and is going to another country, your bank might not likely to let it go through unless you notify them. You also could pay by transferring the money; if you wanted to do that, let me know and I'll send the bank routing numbers.

Have I ever mailed you a packet of information? If not, I would be happy to. It would have sound samples and might give you a better idea as to whether or not the L&C is something you'd like to pursue. Send me your address if you would like more information and I'll get a packet in the mail to you.

I'm sorry for the delay in answering you.

With best wishes,

Hi

I'm in China until Friday and then I go to India until this Monday so I can only get emails but not texts, until then.

Hey, on my 14 hour flight to Beijing, I thought that I'd "take a page out of your book," thinking that some of your discipline rubbed off on me, and skip some of the meals but I only skipped one. I will ask that you don't kill me, but if you must, then I want a kiss just like in all of the movies that I watch.

Exuberance in the air, no impossibility.
Reaganomics won the cold war, restored esprit de corp.
Now we love the takers and drive the makers offshore.
We want all for free, no self-responsibility.
I wish it were again like in the 1980's.

The world was with the USSR.
With Reagan's sunny optimism and 9th inning homers,
Eastern Europe, India, 10724

Gregory Hold

messages.subject: Greg Brown's Weekend Reading and Other Things... 05/05/2013
messages.body:
DEAR FRIEND

After doing a **last review/edit** of my "Weekend Reading" and sending it to friends, being a political news junkie, I start the week with the Sunday Morning major networks news programs. "Face the Nation" hosted by Bob Schieffer/"CBS," "Meet the Press" hosted by David Gregory/"NBC" and "The Week with George Stephanopoulos"/*ABC*. Since in LA they all concurrently broadcast at Bam, I record them along with Chris Matthew's half-hour weekend preview show on "NBC" for later viewing. In addition to their round table panels and subject matter experts, this morning, George W. Bush, New Gingrich, Valerie Jarrett, Chuck Todd, Karl Rove, Bob Woodward, Condoleezza Rice, Michelle Malkin, Dan Rather, David Ignatius, Peggy Noonan, Colbie Roberts, David Brooks, Sam Donaldson, Fareed Zakaria, E.J. Dionne, Jr., Robert Reich, David Gergen, Peggy Noonan, John Dickerson, and Noah O'Donnell, this week's special guests included Senator Lindsey Graham of "CBS," Senator John McCain on "NBC" and Representative Mike Rogers on "ABC," to allow them to Monday Morning quarterback the prior week's news and to offer up to settle scores and advance ideological positions, with sound bites being presented as solutions, pro and con, just in case one is correct. And because great humor is often based on a foundation of truth, by President Obama said at the Press Dinner last Saturday is true that the Sunday news programs "...like to use the Sunday shows to show that they're serious about their commitment to cover all sides of a story, just in case one of them happens to be accurate."

House Intelligence Committee chair Rep. Mike Rogers, R-Mich., said this morning on "This Week" that **some action needs to be taken** against Syria for its alleged use of chemical weapons, saying that the red line** can't be a dotted line.** Sen. Lindsey Graham, R.S.C., said Sunday on "Face the Nation" that **there's a growing consensus in the U.S. Senate** that the United States should get involved. **If we keep this hands-off approach to Syria, this indecisive action towards Syria, kind of not knowing what we're going to do next, we're going to have war with Iran because Iran's going to feel emboldened that we won't act against them for their nuclear weapons program,** he said. **We need to get involved.** And on "Meet the Press," Senator John McCain auguring that the United States should be arming the rebels, using airstrikes to attack Assad's forces and create a safe haven for refugees. What all of this really means, no one knows, because we know from Vietnam, Iraq and Afghanistan, without clearly defined goals and objectives, and a plan to achieve them, any aftertharm will most likely end up as a disaster. The first rule in drinking, **if you don't know sip slow**, and in international diplomacy, **when you don't know move slow.** The President is right to dial back the "red line," especially when none of his options are good and there is no clear long-term goals or strong local partners. Leaving Afghanistan in the hands of Karzai and with Chalabi, Allawi and Maliki has proven to be a disaster. Although I applaud John McCain as a patriot, he is totally out of touch with reality. This is a person who believes that the "surge in Iraq" was a success, when in reality it was a temporary band-aid that for a time, overwhelmed several violent factions while paying off others, but doing nothing to address the underlying core problems and dysfunctionality in the country. So, if we follow his advice and arm the rebels in Syria, it looks like it is going to end up a failed state. As such I believe the tjat Senator McCain and the other Sunday experts are wrong when they insist that American should act alone, when there is nothing that the US can do other than putting a band-aid on a festering situation, especially with little or no public support at home, and regional non-existent partners, and a President's options are bad. Bombing a foreign country is an **act of war,** however you spin it. And as Colin Powell once cautioned, President George W. Bush **if it breaks you will own it**, the same is true in Syria. It is estimated that 70,000 people have already died in Syria as a result of this current civil war, and to use the death of 20 to 30 more as a pretense to escalate a bit higher, is in my opinion, though Sadam was a WMD, less so than Assad, and the world would be a better place without either of them. Still, we couldn't even get background checks approved in Congress last week. I watched the "Sunday Morning News Programs," with their guests advocating that we do something immediately, even when they all agree that there are no good options. Maybe when there are no good options, we should do nothing. **If it is truly a problem, let the EU or the UN to get involved.** But Stewart gave Graham some credit when he said **we just have to get the right weapons to the right people.** Oh, the right weapons to the right people... maybe we
"Nah, that'll never work."
Please watch the above video clip, to truly see the absurdity of the ill-thought advice that the Sunday News Programs experts presents week in and week out.

Actually it was kind of nice to see five Presidents representing both parties, putting aside partisan bickering and pushing over the one thing that everyone could agree, George W. Bush is a true patriot and a good man. And having him there when we was Governor of Texas, I can confirm that from my meetings, it is both. Even after personally believing that Cheney and Bush were responsible for the biggest blunder in American history happen forty years earlier to Nixon as a result of water irregularities in Cook County, like with JFK, I hoped that an injustice might produce something positive, as George W ran on a platform of Compassionate Conservatism. And he might have gotten there if it weren't for Cheney, Rumsfeld, Wolfowitz, Rove and others who subverted the White House for their own purposes. It is hard to imagine how much more damage they could have done if Bush had won a second term. How else can we explain how trillions of dollars were spent or diverted to special interest and the rich with so little to show for it. As Deep Throat use to say, **follow the money**.

The issue is that I really can't whitewash are the failures of his administration, no matter how many supporters try to rewrite history so that his legacy can be redeemed, similar to what has happen with Harry Truman. Like LBJ's legacy will always be linked to Viet Nam, Nixon's to Watergate and Carter's to American hostages in Iran, George W. Bush will and should always be painted with his biggest blunder -- the senseless failed war. When asked what was the biggest problem was when the first Bush administration came into office, his father said, **everything is magnified**. He described having a great day in the White House Press Briefing Room, and his Mother calling to say that she saw him pick his nose while on camera and as a result, she will never be able to face her friends at the hairdressers. - thus both mistakes and/or successes are magnified beyond sensible proportion. But this is not true for the 2nd Iran War.

The difference here is not one of magnification. George W's disastrous war, cost the lives of more than 4000 Americans, hundreds of thousands of Iraqis, made refugees out of millions more, costs trillions of dollars and totally destabilized the entire political balance in the Middle East, for what? To remove one or two foreign policy blunders in the country's history. But even if we cut Iraq out of the equation, his ruinous economic policies of lowering taxes and raising spending taking the country from a $230 billion surplus to a $1 trillion yearly deficit, the gutting of regulatory controls that enabled the housing bubble and Wall Street Depression, poor response to Katrina that left thousands of New Orleans destitute (and the President **Brownie you're doing a good job**), the utter mismanagement of the War in Afghanistan and finally **9/11** (the Bushes knew it's a great country. There are a lot of great families, and it's not just the Kennedys. There are a lot of people out there that are very qualified and we've had enough Bushes.

"No taxation without representation" is a slogan originating during the 1750s and 1760s that summarized a primary grievance of the British colonists in the Thirteen Colonies, which was one of the major causes of the American Revolution. In short, many in those colonies believed that, as they were not directly represented in the distant British Parliament, any laws it passed taxing the colonists (such as the Sugar Act and the Stamp Act) were illegal and unconstitutional. This was a form of tax resistance used in protest of what they believed to be unfair taxation. The battle cry was later used in the creation of the United States. Obviously our current congressional representatives in Washington have lost sight that they serve at the pleasure of the people who voted them into office, and as such ought to enact their wishes.

messages.subject: America's $2 Trillion Underground Economy Says About Jobs
messages.body: This week in *Money Morning**, journalist David Zeiler wrote - *What America's $2 Trillion Underground Economy Says About Jobs*. Although I totally disagree with the premise of his article that Obamacare and other regulations enacted during current administration has caused the US underground economy to balloon to $2 trillion annually. By *underground economy*, Zeiler is talking about all the business activity that is not reported to the government, and includes a growing number of people getting paid for their labor in cash. That means the shadowy figures of the underground economy - the drug dealers, Mafia godfathers and tax cheats - now have a lot more company. But most of these new participants in the underground jobs are middle-class working Americans, who are increasingly taking jobs that pay *under the table* either because nothing else is available or they need a second source of income to make ends meet. America's underground economy is nothing new, but since the Great Recession hit in 2009, experts estimate it has doubled in size, driven by unemployed or underemployed people desperate for income. My belief is that many in the underground economy are folks (like my mother who was a domestic worker for fifty years), including handymen day-laborers, construction workers, childcare workers, illegal aliens and domestic maids like my mother. And most of these people have been trapped in this underground economy for years. The reason why so many paying workers off the books has great appeal to employers, who then can avoid paying benefits and taxes, as well as get around regulations that protect workers' right. And as more people are now working from home or have had to take on second jobs, much of this increased business activity goes unreported. But the balloon is a result of companies moving full-time employees to private contractor status, and the growth of many more working from home. Even the workers getting paid under the table don't get off scot-free. They forfeit contributions to Social Security, which will greatly reduce benefits in their retirement years, and get no healthcare, paid vacation or other benefits. And they often end up with lower average pay to boot. *People who do these types of jobs run the risk of getting exploited with lower pay or not being paid at all,* Laura Gonzalez, professor of personal finance at Texas Tech, told *Money Morning*. There could be more people exploited if more people are forced into this type of economy. *Again,* to suggest that Obamacare and increased regulations caused the underground economy to mushroom over the past couple of years, is a totally fallacy, especially since Obamacare wasn't enacted until January 2013, and many of the regulations that have been put in place have been delayed. In addition, many people's work habits have changed due to opportunities on the Internet and because many companies now outsource former in-house activities both here and abroad, in search of increased profits. And with more than 11 million illegal immigrants that we technically are not allowed to participate in the formal economy, a fast-track to citizenship, could quickly add millions to the tax rolls.

messages.subject: Five myths about electric cars
messages.body: This week in “The Washington Post”, Filmmaker Chris Paine wrote “Five myths about electric cars” – based on his documentaries, “Who Killed the Electric Car?”, “Charge!” and “Revenge of the Electric Car.” He writes this article to counter the debate around electric-car maker Fisker.

Paine says this myth is partly his fault, perpetuated by the title of his 2006 documentary, “Who Killed the Electric Car?” “ Saying that the signs back then weren’t promising, when under pressure from car companies and other lobbyists, California rolled back its Zero-Emission Vehicle mandate, GM halted production of its EV1, and Toyota and Honda quit selling their electric cars. The change in the regulation freed car-makers to round up the cars they had leased – and then surreptitiously crush them. Today, almost all the major automakers, along with a cast of new players, are investing in and building plug-in cars. California’s mandate has also made a comeback, and other states are considering similar rules. A new report from IEE, part of the MIT Energy Initiative, predicts that electric vehicles and plug-in electric cars will be on U.S. roads by 2035. “The electrification of the vehicle fleet is a foregone conclusion,” says former GM vice chairman (and former electric-car-basher) Bob Lutz. Having driven both the Fisker and its main start-up rival Tesla, I found both to have the feel of toys, except that Tesla developed both a sports car along with a separate sedan, and is estimated to turn a quarterly profit this year.

But ask people what their biggest hesitation is about electric vehicles, they’re most likely to say something about the cars leaving them stranded. This myth is pervasive throughout the Model T era. My own car, a 2008 Prius plug-in, which I drive in February of Tesla’s Model S, which ended up needing a tow to a charging station, seemed to confirm the fear. But that test drive – covering more than 500 miles in temperatures as low as 10 degrees – was no way your everyday trip. The average American drives fewer than 40 miles a day. The Nissan Leaf, with a range of more than 70 miles, and Tesla’s Model S can go as far as 265 miles on a single charge. The Toyota Prius Plug-in and the Ford C-Max Energi all use electric power for the first 20 to 30 miles and then switch to gasoline for longer drives. And most Americans drive less than 40 miles a day.

Charging an electric car can be as simple as plugging it into a wall outlet. But AC outlet charging is slow, taking between eight and 24 hours. So it’s not usually the method of first resort. That’s why most plug-in cars are sold with charging docks that work in a home garage and can charge a car in four to eight hours, allowing drivers to treat their cars like their cellphones: topping them off periodically or charging them up overnight.

It is also associated with the Gaelic Beltane. And many of the pagan celebrations were abandoned or Christianized during the process of conversion in Europe. The modern observance of May Day began with the May Day protests and rallies in Chicago decided to designate May 1, 1886 as a day of national demonstration to campaign for an eight-hour work day. *May Day* was formalized as an international holiday in Paris. It has since become an official holiday in many countries where governments respect the will of working people.
